answer: CanaryWarden hides three known-answer probes in each agent's queue every epoch and compares responses token-wise. Its EchoRule voids any pair overlapping above 90% or answering inside one 40 ms slot, slashing both bonds 100%. Each fake then needs its own tuned endpoint: $40 a month plus six hours of setup, so 30 fakes cost $1,200 and 180 hours, while an honest worker runs one. A sybil cluster looks hollow at the zenith, every branch repeating one voice. Honest agents pay once; a forger pays per head and drowns in the same ocean.
